findings.description: Priority 1 recommendation bullets are generic, lacking any specific data anchor from the audit (e.g., selector, count, URL). The advice "Give every custom control an accessible name and the correct role…" is a copy‑paste style statement that could apply to any site.

Priority 2 recommendation bullets are generic, lacking specific selectors or counts. Advice such as "Raise the contrast ratio of the flagged text…" does not reference any particular element from the audit data.
Priority 3 recommendation bullets are generic and do not include a selector, count, or page URL. The guidance to expose structure via native elements is a standard best‑practice statement.
Priority 4 recommendation bullets are generic; they advise adding a submit button without specifying where or how many instances were found in the audit.
Priority 5 recommendation bullets are generic, lacking any selector or count. The suggestion to add descriptive alt text is a blanket statement.
Priority 6 recommendation bullets are generic and do not reference specific heading levels or counts from the audit data.
Priority 7 recommendation bullets are generic; they advise adding a <main> landmark without citing any page URL or element count.
Priority 8 recommendation bullets are generic, lacking selectors or counts. The advice to replace naked containers with semantic elements is a standard recommendation not tied to audit data.
Priority 9 recommendation bullets are generic; they advise adding missing security headers without referencing any specific header names or audit findings beyond the absence of those headers.
Priority 10 recommendation bullets are generic and do not include a selector, count, or page URL. The guidance to add required Schema.org properties is a blanket statement.
Priority 11 recommendation bullets are generic; they advise publishing llms.txt without specifying any file path or audit evidence beyond its absence.
Priority 12 recommendation bullets are generic and do not reference any specific sitemap entries or counts. The advice to publish a sitemap.xml is a standard best‑practice statement.
